scope: Follow-up to docs/binius-commit-prove-research.json. That experiment found proving SHA256(seed)=commitment instead of the full SHA-512/clamp/scalar-mult relation barely shrank the Binius64 Iron Spartan proof, because both relations' AND-constraint counts padded to the identical 2048-word trace bucket. A probe over already-vetted 32-byte hash gadgets in binius-circuits found BLAKE3 needs only 626 AND constraints versus SHA-256's 912, landing in a 1024-word bucket -- half of SHA-256's. This experiment measures what that actually does to proof size/time, proving BLAKE3(seed)=commitment against the identical pinned Binius64 commit, Iron Spartan configuration and action-binding discipline. BLAKE3 is an already-implemented, independently specified hash, chosen only because it is the smallest already-vetted gadget available, not proposed as a production commitment function. Public fixture only; not a production relation, not a security approval.

wrong_witness_measurement.scope: Actual unsatisfied-witness prover abort; NOT verifier rejection of an adversarially generated proof. Identical failure phase/exit code to both other comparators' own wrong-witness measurements.

proof_size_vs_trace_size.scope: Three measured points at log_inv_rate=1, SECURITY_BITS=96 on the identical pinned backend, ordered by committed_total_len.
proof_size_vs_trace_size.observation: Halving committed_total_len (2048 to 1024, i.e. removing exactly one bit from log2(committed_total_len)) halved setup time (~0.80s average of the two 2048-word points to 0.41s) but only shrank proof bytes by about 4.4% (539,872-byte average to 515,984). This is the expected shape for a FRI/BaseFold-style argument: setup/preprocessing cost scales with the trace size itself (O(n)), while proof bytes scale with the number of FRI queries times the Merkle-authentication-path length, i.e. O(queries * log(n) * hash_size) -- one fewer Merkle-tree level per query (log2(n) dropping from 11 to 10) removes a small, roughly constant amount per query across a FIXED query count (232 per pins.json), not a share proportional to n itself.

conclusion: Crossing into a smaller power-of-two trace bucket via a smaller already-vetted hash gadget (BLAKE3 instead of SHA-256) IS measurably effective for CPU time (prove -29%, verify -22%, setup -52% relative to the SHA-256 comparator) but only modestly effective for proof SIZE (-4.4%), because this backend's proof size is dominated by a term that scales with log(trace size), not trace size itself. This means relation-size reduction alone, even successfully crossing a padding bucket boundary, cannot deliver the order-of-magnitude proof-size reduction F-01 needs under this backend's FRI/BaseFold construction -- confirming (with a direct measurement on this exact pinned dependency, not an assumption) that closing F-01's size side needs a backend whose proof size does not scale this way, such as a lattice-based construction (LaBinius+LaBRADOR, Cyclo, RoKoko; see docs/COMPACT_BACKEND_LATTICE_GATE.md section 3), rather than further relation shrinking on the current backend.
